title: ~아/어 놓다 [a/eo notda] (To have done something in advance)
shortExplanation: Used to indicate that an action was performed ahead of time in preparation for something else.
longExplanation: '~아/어 놓다 [a/eo notda]' is used to express that an action has been done beforehand—either to prepare for a future event or to leave something in a completed state. This form is common in everyday conversation and adds nuance to your sentence structure.

examples.sentence: 나는 내일 아침에 바쁠 것을 생각하고 오늘 저녁에 아침 식사를 만들어 놓았어요.
examples.romanization: Naneun naeil achime bappeul geoseu saenggakago oneul jeonyeoge achim siksareul mandeureo noasseoyo.
examples.translation: I made breakfast tonight in anticipation of being busy tomorrow morning.

examples.sentence: 시험 준비를 위해 이번 주 동안 모든 강의 노트를 미리 쓰고 놓았어요.
examples.romanization: Siheom junbireul wihae ibeon ju dongan modeun gangui noteureul miri sseo noasseoyo.
examples.translation: I wrote all my lecture notes in advance this week to prepare for the exam.

examples.sentence: 우리는 피서 가기 전에 집안 청소를 하고 놓았어요.
examples.romanization: Ulineun pisoga gagi jeone jipan cheongsoreul hago noasseoyo.
examples.translation: We cleaned the house in preparation for our vacation.

examples.sentence: 오늘은 친구들이 와서 미리 음식을 만들어 놓을 거예요.
examples.romanization: Oneuleun chingudeuli waseo miri eumsigeul mandeureo noheul geoyeyo.
examples.translation: My friends are coming over today, so I'm going to prepare the food in advance.

title: ~아/어 달라다 [a/eo dallada] (To ask for)
shortExplanation: Used to make a request or ask someone to do something.
longExplanation: '~아/어 달라다 [a/eo dallada]' is a form derived from the verb '달라하다' used when requesting or asking someone to do something. It is formed by conjugating the verb into its 아/어 form and then adding 달라다.

examples.sentence: 제 친구가 매우 배가 고파서, '빨리 밥을 줘 달라'고 말했어요.
examples.romanization: Je chinguga maeu baega gopaseo, 'ppalli babeul jwo dalla'go malhaesseoyo.
examples.translation: My friend was very hungry, so he asked, 'Give me food quickly.'

examples.sentence: 머리가 너무 아파서, '약 좀 주어 달라'고 요청했어요.
examples.romanization: Meoriga neomu apaseo, 'yak jom jueo dalla'go yocheonghaesseoyo.
examples.translation: I had a severe headache, so I asked for some medicine.

examples.sentence: 집이 너무 더워서, '에어컨 좀 틀어 달라'고 부탁했어요.
examples.romanization: Jibi neomu deoweoseo, 'eokon jom teureo dalla'go butakhaesseoyo.
examples.translation: It was so hot in the house, so I asked, 'Please turn on the air conditioner.'

examples.sentence: 커피가 너무 맛있어서, '한 잔만 더 줘 달라'고 말했어요.
examples.romanization: Keopiga neomu masisseoseo, 'han janman deo jwo dalla'go malhaesseoyo.
examples.translation: The coffee was so delicious that I asked, 'Please give me one more cup.'

title: ~아/어 대다 [a/eo daeda] (To do aimlessly)
shortExplanation: Used to indicate that an action is done without a clear purpose or merely out of idleness.
longExplanation: '~아/어 대다 [a/eo daeda]' attaches to a verb stem to express that the action is performed aimlessly, without proper thought, or in an idle, unproductive manner.

examples.sentence: 제가 그냥 막 쇼핑을 하다 대다 결국 비싼 옷을 샀어요.
examples.romanization: Jega geunyang mak syoping-eul hada daeda gyeolguk bissan os-eul sass-eoyo.
examples.translation: I was shopping around aimlessly and ended up buying expensive clothes.

examples.sentence: 시험기간이지만 그는 그냥 책을 들여다보다 대다 시간을 다 보냈어요.
examples.romanization: Siheomgiganijiman geuneun geunyang chaeg-eul deulyeodaboda daeda sigan-eul da bonaess-eoyo.
examples.translation: Even though it was exam period, he just idly looked at his books and passed the time.

examples.sentence: 소리를 들으면서 그녀는 그냥 거리를 걷다 대다 음식점을 놓쳤어요.
examples.romanization: Soli reul deureumyeonseo geunyeoneun geunyang georireul geotda daeda eumsikjeom-eul nohchyeoss-eoyo.
examples.translation: While listening to music, she was aimlessly walking down the street and missed the restaurant.

examples.sentence: 나는 지루해서 그냥 인터넷을 서핑하다 대다 알게 된 사이트에서 책을 구입했다.
examples.romanization: Naneun jiluhaeseo geunyang inteonet-eul seopinghada daeda alge doen saiteu-eseo chaeg-eul gu-ibhaetda.
examples.translation: Bored, I was aimlessly surfing the internet and ended up buying a book from a site I found.

title: ~아/어 보이다 [a/eo boida] (To seem, appear)
shortExplanation: Used to express that something appears or seems to be a certain way.
longExplanation: The grammar point '~아/어 보이다 [a/eo boida]' is used to indicate that something looks or appears a certain way according to the speaker's perception or judgment. It is often used to describe appearances, conditions, or states based on external observation.

examples.sentence: 그 여자는 매우 행복해 보이는데, 실제로는 아마 막대한 스트레스를 받고 있을 것 같아요.
examples.romanization: Geu yeojaneun maeu haengbokhae boineunde, siljero-neun ama makdaehan seuteureseuleul badgo isseul geos gatayo.
examples.translation: That woman seems very happy, but in reality, she is probably under a lot of stress.

examples.sentence: 오늘은 날씨가 참 좋아 보이네요, 외출하기에 좋은 날인 것 같아요.
examples.romanization: Oneuleun nalssiga cham joah boineyo, oechulhagi-e joheun narin geos gatayo.
examples.translation: The weather seems really nice today; it appears to be a good day to go out.

examples.sentence: 이 케이크는 달해 보이지만, 실제로는 그렇게 달지 않아요.
examples.romanization: Ii keikeuneun dalhae boijiman, siljero-neun geureoke dalji anhayo.
examples.translation: This cake seems sweet, but it isn’t actually that sweet.

examples.sentence: 나는 피곤해 보인다고 친구가 말했어요, 하지만 저는 그렇게 느낀 적이 없어요.
examples.romanization: Naneun pigonhae boindago chinguga malhaesseoyo, hajiman jeoneun geureoke neukkin jeogi eobseoyo.
examples.translation: My friend said I looked tired, but I’ve never felt that way.

title: ~아/어 서는 [a/eo seoneun] (Although)
shortExplanation: Used to express a contrast or contrary expectation; 'although' or 'but'.
longExplanation: '~아/어 서는 [a/eo seoneun]' is used to present a situation that contrasts with or contradicts an expectation. It can be translated as 'although' or 'but' and highlights an unexpected or contrary fact.

examples.sentence: 날씨가 춥다고 해서는 외출을 안 했는데, 실제로는 그리 춥지 않았어요.
examples.romanization: Nalssiga chubdago haeseoneun oechuleul an haenneunde, siljero-neun geuri chubji anhasseoyo.
examples.translation: Although they said it was cold, I didn’t go out; in fact, it wasn’t that cold.

examples.sentence: 헬스장에 자주 가서는 운동을 열심히 했는데, 체중은 거의 줄지 않았어요.
examples.romanization: Helthjange jaju gaseoneun undongeul yeolsimhi haenneunde, chejungeun geojeul julji anhasseoyo.
examples.translation: Although I went to the gym frequently and worked out hard, my weight barely decreased.

examples.sentence: 열심히 공부해서는 시험을 잘 보려고 했는데, 결과는 좋지 않았어요.
examples.romanization: Yeolsimhi gongbuhaseoneun siheomeul jal boryeogo haenneunde, gyulegwaneun joaji anhasseoyo.
examples.translation: Although I studied hard to do well on the exam, the result wasn’t good.

examples.sentence: 저는 열심히 외워서는 공연 때 잘 했다고 생각했는데, 실수를 많이 했어요.
examples.romanization: Jeoneun yeolsimhi weowoseoneun gongyeon ttae jal haetdago saenggakhaenneunde, silsureul mani haesseoyo.
examples.translation: Although I memorized it thoroughly and thought I did well during the performance, I ended up making many mistakes.

title: ~아/어야만 [a/eoyaman] (Only if/when)
shortExplanation: Used to express a condition that only if/when something happens, something else will or can occur.
longExplanation: The phrase '~아/어야만' is a conditional form in Korean that expresses the idea that only if/when a certain condition is satisfied can an expected result occur. This grammar point indicates that an action or state is contingent on a condition being fulfilled; without that condition, the action or state is impossible. It is often used with potential or hypothetical situations.
formation: Verb + 아/어야만 (Depending on the final vowel of the verb stem)

examples.sentence: 고등학교를 졸업해야만 대학교에 들어갈 수 있어요.
examples.romanization: Godeunghakgyoreul joreobhaeyaman daehakgyoe deuleogal su isseoyo.
examples.translation: You can only go to university if you graduate from high school.

examples.sentence: 그 영화를 위해 꼭 티켓을 예약해야만 볼 수 있어요.
examples.romanization: Geu yeonghwareul wihae ggok tikeseul yeyakhaeyaman bol su isseoyo.
examples.translation: You can only watch that movie if you book the tickets in advance.

examples.sentence: 목표를 이루려면 하루하루 열심히 일해야만 해요.
examples.romanization: Mokpyoreul iruryeomyeon haruharu yeolsimhi ilhaeyaman haeyo.
examples.translation: In order to achieve your goal, you have to work hard every day.

examples.sentence: 거기에 가려면 버스를 타야만 해요, 지하철로는 갈 수 없어요.
examples.romanization: Geogie garyeomyeon beoseureul taya haeyaman haeyo, jihacheoroneun gal su eopsseoyo.
examples.translation: To get there, you have to take a bus; it's not possible to go by subway.

title: ~아/어지다 [a/eojida] (To become)
shortExplanation: Used to express a change of state, meaning 'to become'.
longExplanation: '~아/어지다' is a verb ending used in Korean to indicate a change in state, condition, or emotion—essentially, 'to become'. The ending is chosen based on the vowel in the preceding syllable (use '아지다' after ㅏ or ㅗ, and '어지다' for all other vowels). It is often used to show a transition from one state to another.

examples.sentence: 날씨가 갑자기 추워져서 난로를 켜야 했어요.
examples.romanization: Nalssiga gapjagi chuweojyeoseo nanroleul kyeoya haesseoyo.
examples.translation: The weather suddenly became cold, so I had to turn on the heater.

examples.sentence: 작년에는 일을 너무 많이 해서 피곤해서 쉴 시간이 없어져서 힘들었어요.
examples.romanization: Jaknyeoneun ireul neomu manihaseo pigonhaeseo swil sigan-i eobseojyeoseo himdeureoss-eoyo.
examples.translation: Last year, I worked so much that I became tired and had no time to rest, so it was tough.

examples.sentence: 친구가 바빠지니까 자주 만날 수 없게 됐어요.
examples.romanization: Chinguga bappajinikkaji jaju mannal su eobge dwaesseoyo.
examples.translation: Since my friend became busy, we couldn't meet as often.

examples.sentence: 음식이 너무 많아져서 한 번에 다 먹을 수 없었어요.
examples.romanization: Eumsigi neomu manhajyeoseo han beone da meogeul su eopseosseoyo.
examples.translation: The food became so abundant that I couldn't eat it all at once.

title: ~았/었 던 [at/eot deon] (Past descriptive)
shortExplanation: Used to describe past events or situations from the speaker's memory.
longExplanation: '~았/었 던' is a past descriptive form in Korean used to recall an event, person, or situation that occurred in the past. It is commonly attached to a verb (forming '보던') when modifying a noun and expresses a past state or memory from the speaker’s perspective.
formation: Verb in past tense (~았/었) + 던 (attached before a noun)

examples.sentence: 제가 어릴 때 즐겨 보던 애니메이션 쇼를 어제 다시 보았어요, 많은 추억이 떠올랐어요.
examples.romanization: Jega eoril ttae jeulgyeo bodon aenimeisyeon syoreul eoje dasi boasseoyo, manheun chueogi tteooreosseoyo.
examples.translation: I watched the animation show I used to enjoy as a kid again yesterday, and many memories came flooding back.

examples.sentence: 그는 5년 전에 만났던 친구와 오랜만에 다시 만났어요.
examples.romanization: Geuneun 5nyeon jeone mannatdeon chinguwa oraenman-e dasi mannatseoyo.
examples.translation: He met a friend he had met 5 years ago after a long time.

examples.sentence: 여름에 가봤던 해변에 다시 가고 싶어요.
examples.romanization: Yeoreum-e gabwatdeon haebyeone dasi gago sipeoyo.
examples.translation: I want to go back to the beach I visited in the summer.

examples.sentence: 저는 학교에서 만났던 친구들과 지금도 친하게 지내요.
examples.romanization: Jeoneun hakgyoeso mannatdeon chingudeulgwa jigeumdo chinhage jinaeyo.
examples.translation: I am still close with the friends I met at school.

title: ~았/었으면 좋겠다 [at/eosseumyeon jokgetda] (Wish something had happened)
shortExplanation: Used to express a wish or hope that something had occurred in the past.
longExplanation: '~았/었으면 좋겠다' is a grammar construction in Korean that expresses a speaker's wish or regret about a past event that did not occur. By combining a verb in the past tense with '으면 좋겠다', it conveys a longing for a different past outcome.

examples.sentence: 회사에 보고하러 갔었으면 좋겠다, 그러면 지금 이렇지 않았을 텐데.
examples.romanization: Hoesae bogoharerogasseosseumyeon jokgetda, geureomyeon jigeum ireotji anhasseultende.
examples.translation: I wish I had gone to report to the company; then I wouldn't be like this now.

examples.sentence: 당신을 더 일찍 알았었으면 좋겠다, 그렇게 되면 많은 문제를 피할 수 있었을 텐데.
examples.romanization: Dangsineul deo iljjik arasseosseumyeon jokgetda, geureohge doemyeon manheun munjeleul pihal su isseosseultende.
examples.translation: I wish I had known you sooner; then I could have avoided many problems.

examples.sentence: 난 그날 그를 따랐었으면 좋겠다, 그러면 어떤 경험을 할 수 있었을까?
examples.romanization: Nan geunal geuleul ttaratseosseumyeon jokgetda, geureomyeon eoddeon gyeongheomeul hal su isseosseulkka?
examples.translation: I wish I had followed him that day—what kind of experience would I have had?

examples.sentence: 더 많은 연습을 했었으면 좋겠다, 그래야 내 성과가 더욱 개선될 수 있었을 텐데.
examples.romanization: Deo manheun yeonseubeul haesseosseumyeon jokgetda, geuraeya nae seonggwaga deouk gaeseondwaesseultende.
examples.translation: I wish I had practiced more, then my performance could have improved even further.
